summary: Design is well-structured and identifies the root cause correctly, but contains 1 HIGH-severity gap and 9 MEDIUM-severity ambiguities that must be resolved before implementation. All findings are concrete and actionable.

findings.title: Ambiguous Header-to-Field Resolution Order — May Produce Incorrect Matches
findings.problem: The resolution algorithm's pseudocode does not clarify precedence between canonical-name matches and label matches. When both could apply, it's unclear which wins. The pseudocode also does not clearly show ambiguity detection when multiple fields could match.
findings.concrete_fix: Provide explicit pseudocode with clear precedence: (1) canonical names, (2) labels, (3) formatting equivalence. Show how ambiguity is detected. Include decision matrix or flowchart.

findings.title: Contradictory Treatment of Spaces/Underscores in Normalization
findings.problem: The design defines two normalization functions but doesn't clearly state when each is applied. Example: does 'customer name' (with space) match 'customer_name' (with underscore) in step 2 or step 3? The pseudocode is ambiguous.
findings.concrete_fix: Explicitly define when each normalization function is applied. Either apply _normalize_for_comparison() upfront to all headers, or show clear pseudocode for when each normalization is used.

findings.title: Missing Specification for Building Lookup Tables in __init__
findings.problem: The __init__ method calls _build_lookup_tables() which is never defined. The structure of _field_by_label (single field vs. list of fields for ambiguous labels) is unclear.
findings.concrete_fix: Add explicit pseudocode for _build_lookup_tables() showing how lookup tables are initialized, how ambiguous labels are stored, and how they're handled during resolution.

findings.title: Unclear Error Message for Duplicate Columns
findings.location: Design section 3: resolve_headers error messages for duplicates
findings.problem: The error message format for duplicates references 'seen_canonical' but doesn't specify what this stores. The pseudocode doesn't clearly track the original CSV header that caused each duplicate.
findings.concrete_fix: Explicitly define seen_canonical as mapping canonical_field_name to original_raw_csv_header. Update pseudocode to show tracking and error message formatting clearly.

findings.title: Frontend Implementation Option Not Decided
findings.location: Design section 5: Frontend Integration — Option A vs. Option B
findings.problem: Design offers two options (backend endpoint vs. TypeScript reimplementation) but chooses Option B without justifying the choice or addressing synchronization risks. If Python and TypeScript implementations diverge, preview and import will behave differently.
findings.concrete_fix: Either recommend Option A (backend validation endpoint) to eliminate sync issues, or if Option B is chosen, add explicit requirements: maintain single source of truth, add regression tests comparing both implementations, update both in same PR.

findings.title: Empty/Malformed CSV Handling Not Fully Specified
findings.location: Design section 3: error handling for empty/whitespace headers
findings.problem: Design handles empty files and missing headers, but doesn't specify behavior for headers that are entirely whitespace after trimming (e.g., '  ' or tab character).
findings.concrete_fix: Add explicit handling for empty headers in resolve_headers pseudocode. Add Test Case 21: CSV with whitespace-only column header is rejected with 'Empty column header' error.

findings.title: Row-Level Error Handling vs. Header Validation Interaction Not Specified
findings.location: Design section 2 and 3: transition from header validation to row processing
findings.problem: Design doesn't clarify the contract between header resolution and row validation. After header validation succeeds, are we guaranteed that all row keys will be valid canonical names? What if an edge case introduces a key that wasn't validated?
findings.concrete_fix: Add note clarifying: (1) All keys in header_mapping are guaranteed valid canonical names, (2) Remapped rows will only contain keys in schema, (3) Row validation's 'unknown field' check is redundant but acts as safety net. Verify this in code.

findings.title: Test Case 17 (Preview-Backend Consistency) Lacks Specification
findings.location: Requirements section, Acceptance criteria, Test Case 17
findings.problem: Test case 17 is vague: 'verify identical header-resolution rules' but doesn't specify test inputs, expected outputs, or how to measure consistency. If Option B (TypeScript) is used, consistency is not automatically guaranteed.
findings.concrete_fix: Expand Test Case 17 with explicit test inputs, expected outputs, and verification steps. If Option B is used, add test that calls both Python and TypeScript resolvers with identical input and asserts outputs are identical.

findings.title: Design Does Not Reference Actual API_CONTRACTS.md Endpoint Specification
findings.location: Design overview and section 1: Backend Flow
findings.problem: Design describes modifying the import endpoint but doesn't cite or verify against the actual API_CONTRACTS.md section 5.10. Doesn't confirm error response format matches contract or whether new error codes require contract updates.
findings.concrete_fix: Add section 'API Contract Verification' that cites section 5.10, confirms request/response formats remain unchanged, and documents new error codes (UNKNOWN_COLUMN, DUPLICATE_COLUMN, AMBIGUOUS_HEADER) to be added to API_CONTRACTS.md.

findings.title: Missing Specification for Validation of Multiple Entity Types
findings.location: Requirements section, Acceptance criteria, Test Case 14
findings.problem: Test Case 14 (universal solution for multiple CRMs) is vague. Doesn't specify which CRM types to test, field overlaps, or whether resolver is properly scoped per entity.
findings.concrete_fix: Expand Test Case 14 with specific CRM configurations (different field names, overlapping field names, ambiguous labels) and verify that each CRM's resolver is independent.

findings.title: Performance Claim Not Validated Against Implementation
findings.problem: Design claims header resolution completes in '< 1ms' for typical CSVs but provides no benchmark. The pseudocode is O(n*m) which should be verified empirically.
findings.concrete_fix: Either add a performance benchmark test case (e.g., 100 headers, 100 fields) to the test suite, or replace the specific '< 1ms' claim with a less specific statement like 'Performs well for typical CSVs and entities'.

findings.title: Frontend TypeScript Implementation Skeleton Not Provided
findings.problem: Design provides incomplete pseudocode for TypeScript resolver. Comment says 'Implement same normalization and resolution logic' but doesn't specify what that logic is. Could lead to divergence.
findings.concrete_fix: If Option B (TypeScript implementation) is chosen, provide complete pseudocode for TypeScript version. Otherwise, defer detail to implementation and add explicit requirement to sync both versions.

verified_assumptions.assumption: Field labels and canonical names exist in the schema
verified_assumptions.evidence: backend/app/schemas/crm.py: CRMField has both 'name' (lowercase identifier) and 'label' (string, 1-100 chars)

verified_assumptions.assumption: Current backend validation compares CSV headers directly against canonical names without normalization
verified_assumptions.evidence: backend/app/routers/records.py lines 250-254: field_names = {f.name for f in entity.fields}; csv_fields = set(reader.fieldnames or []); unknown_fields = csv_fields - field_names

verified_assumptions.assumption: Frontend CSV preview does not validate headers
verified_assumptions.evidence: frontend/src/features/records/CSVImportModal.tsx lines 40-60: handleFileChange() parses CSV without header normalization

verified_assumptions.assumption: Existing validate_csv_row() works with canonical field names
verified_assumptions.evidence: backend/app/services/validation.py line 155+: Checks row keys against field_map (canonical names)

verified_assumptions.assumption: API response format for import is {created, skipped, errors}
verified_assumptions.evidence: backend/app/routers/records.py lines 288-294: success_response includes created, skipped, errors

verified_assumptions.assumption: Authorization checks enforced in import endpoint
File size and row count limits already enforced
verified_assumptions.evidence: backend/app/routers/records.py: MAX_CSV_SIZE = 5MB, MAX_CSV_ROWS = 10000, validation checks present

unverified_assumptions.assumption: Display labels are unique within an entity (enforced by schema validation)
unverified_assumptions.evidence: Design claims uniqueness is enforced in backend/app/schemas/crm.py, but no explicit validator found that enforces label uniqueness
unverified_assumptions.impact: If labels are not unique, resolver's ambiguity handling becomes critical but is unclear (see Finding #1)

unverified_assumptions.assumption: Frontend can call backend validation endpoint or re-implement resolver
unverified_assumptions.evidence: No preview endpoint exists in codebase. Design proposes two options but doesn't commit to either
unverified_assumptions.impact: Implementation path unclear until approach is decided

unverified_assumptions.assumption: Preview and import use different parsing logic
unverified_assumptions.evidence: Frontend uses string.split(); backend uses csv.DictReader()
unverified_assumptions.impact: Design correctly identifies this as source of inconsistency

blocking_issues: Finding #1: HIGH severity — ambiguous resolution algorithm must be clarified
Finding #5: MEDIUM severity — frontend approach (Option A vs B) must be decided
recommendations: Before implementation, resolve findings #1–5 with design author
Add explicit test fixtures and data for findings #6–10
Make explicit frontend decision: backend endpoint or TypeScript reimplementation
Verify label uniqueness enforcement in schema validation
Add cross-language test for Python/TypeScript resolver consistency
